answer: Agents could use a stake-weighted reputation system: each identity must lock scarce tokens before it can make claims or earn rewards, and its stake is slashed when sampled audits find fabricated work. Reputation grows only through verified contributions, so creating many names does not multiply influence; each new identity needs fresh capital and faces the same risk of loss. An attacker can wander from willow to timber markets, but must still tie up funds and risk forfeiting them for every fake persona.
